subject: Urgent: OrchidPay throughput collapse after quant profile change
messages:
From: Julia Wang <julia.wang@orchidpay.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: Throughput and error spike in production after model update

Hi Naomi,

We observed a dramatic drop in throughput and a surge in 5xx errors starting ~07:15 local after your team pushed what we were told was a quant profile update for model assignment to our /generate endpoint (version: rwinf-v2.1-quant). P95 latency jumped from ~280ms to >2.4s and many requests started returning 502/504.

We attached a small sample of logs and a timing trace. Key observations from our side:
- Request rate is the same as prior hour (~400 req/s) but tail latency spiked and most requests were being retried by our client.
- Memory spikes on the serving nodes prior to errors (see orchid_logs_1130.tar.gz).
- No config changes on our side.

This is impacting our checkout flow in production. Can you triage immediately and advise rollback options? We are prepared to accept a short maintenance window.

Attachments: orchid_logs_1130.tar.gz, timing_trace_1130.jsonl

Regards,
Julia Wang
Senior PM, Orchids & Payments
OrchidPay
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Julia Wang <julia.wang@orchidpay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 08:25:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Throughput and error spike in production after model update

Julia —

Thanks for the quick flag and the logs. We see the same symptom set in our telemetry. I’m escalating to infra and runtime immediately (cc’d).

Proposed immediate plan (can start in the next 5–10 minutes if you approve):
1) Canary rollback of assignment for your tenant to rwinf-v2.0-quant on 2 nodes so we can validate latency recovery.
2) Enable request throttling (rate cap) at edge for your API key to prevent client retries from overwhelming the cluster while rollback proceeds.
3) Collect full KV/embedding cache dumps and a longer trace — we’ll send a short request template (orchid_trace_request.md) for any additional logs we need from you.

Please confirm rollback approval and an acceptable maintenance window (we suggest a 2-hour window to finish validation and run a controlled patch if needed). We will also prepare a short incident note for your customers.

I’ll coordinate updates in this thread.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 08:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Throughput and error spike in production after model update

Naomi / team —

Quick diagnostic from the serving layer: after the quant profile change the memory allocation pattern for KV cache entries shifted — we’re seeing a ~30% increase in per-request KV memory and a small but crucial change in alignment that causes larger-than-expected copies on CPU-bound paths. That triggers GC pressure and increases tail latency; once the queue grows we start seeing 502/504 from the edge.

Immediate recommendations:
- APPROVE rollback to rwinf-v2.0-quant for OrchidPay assignment (should be instantaneous at the routing layer).
- We’ll also push a small runtime fix to avoid the alignment-induced copies (hotfix) but that requires a build-and-deploy (ETA ~45 minutes).
- In parallel we should disable the new quant profile for the global model catalog and add an ABORT flag for any scheduled auto-rollouts.

I’ll start the rollback as soon as Naomi confirms customer approval. Attaching the snippet of the memory profile we’re seeing: timing_trace_1130.jsonl

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Julia Wang <julia.wang@orchidpay.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Throughput and error spike in production after model update

Naomi —

Operational notes / asks for approval:
- Canary rollback: immediate, no DB migration, very low risk. We recommend running it behind a 2-hour maintenance window to allow for extended validation and to monitor for downstream effects.
- Hotfix deployment: will take ~45 minutes once baked in CI; we prefer to deploy after rollback to avoid introducing variables during smoke tests.
- SLA/credits: given the customer impact, recommend offering a goodwill credit (we should consult finance/legal) and preemptively draft an incident note for their customers.

If you have customer approval I will trigger the rollback and keep watch from the runtime side. Also looping Product Ops if we need to lock the model catalog rollout.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Runtime, Redwood Inference
From: Julia Wang <julia.wang@orchidpay.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Throughput and error spike in production after model update

Naomi / Marcus / Rishi —

Thank you. We approve the canary rollback immediately and the 2-hour maintenance window (09:20–11:20 EST). Please proceed with rollback first and then run the hotfix only after you confirm recovery.

A couple of quick asks:
- Were any inference payloads or customer PII logged during the spike? We need an initial answer for our security/compliance team.
- Please confirm whether the rollback will change any request IDs so our tracing correlators don’t break.

We’ll standby and provide additional logs if you need them.

—Julia
Julia Wang
Senior PM, OrchidPay
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Julia Wang <julia.wang@orchidpay.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:20:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Throughput and error spike in production after model update — rollback approved and next steps

Julia —

Rollback approved and in progress. Summary of actions (mutual action plan):
- 09:20: Canary rollback of OrchidPay assignment to rwinf-v2.0-quant initiated by Marcus.
- 09:22: Edge rate-limiting set to 600 req/s to prevent retry storms.
- 09:30: Expecting latency and error metrics to normalize; Rishi will verify memory profile and report back.
- 10:15: If stable for 30m, schedule hotfix deploy with a 45-minute bake window; otherwise we’ll extend investigation.

Quick answers to security/compliance: no customer PII was written to any long-term log store; traces and timings are sampled and ephemeral. We will provide a short compliance note once Rishi confirms the collected artifacts. We will not change request IDs during rollback — only routing to a prior model assignment.

Attachments: orchid_trace_request.md (request for additional logs if needed).

I’ll update this thread when we have recovery metrics. Thanks for the quick approval.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
